expects.rule: The full name of the school or university is prominent on every page, not only in the footer.
All programmes or courses are listed with their names visible, grouped by field if needed: 48% of tested users did not realise a school offered the programme they wanted.
Application deadlines, a step-by-step application process and outcome figures (job placement) are easy to find and labelled with numbers and sources.
Images are authentic (real students, real classrooms) rather than stock photos, and the About page gives a scannable list of facts in plain language.
Prospective students and parents can see who teaches: faculty or teacher pages with names and backgrounds.
Body text and controls meet WCAG AA contrast: at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.
A course page shows duration, price, schedule, level and what the learner can do afterwards, with one clear enrol or enquire button.
A site search that works, because users often arrive from search engines and look for one programme or date.

traits: 6 of 7 first screens carry one main action (Inquire, Find a school, Join waitlist, Download app, Explore), none carries more than two.

5 of 6 seen on a screenshot lead with a photograph or video of real people (child on a balance beam, children in a line, a barista, a phone on a desk); Krackerz uses four photo cards and CalArts uses none.
Headlines are 10 words or fewer on 6 of 7 (Seen & valued, Speak like you mean it, Bettr Coffee. Bettr World.), set at 36 to 198 px.
5 of 6 use one or two typefaces, usually a display face for the headline and a plain sans for the rest (Jobclarendon + Roboto, DM Sans + Inter, Sirca + Soehne).
The first screen holds fewer than 40 words of text on 5 of 6 seen on a screenshot.
Page backgrounds split: 3 of 6 dark or black (Bettr, Fluently, CalArts), 3 of 6 light or cream; each uses one saturated accent (yellow, lime, violet).
Parent-facing school sites (Quaker School, Primer) put approach, support, admissions or tuition in the top menu; course platforms put audience or price instead.

sites.name: Bettr Academy
sites.why: Full-bleed dimmed photograph of an espresso machine and a hand holding a milk jug; headline 'Bettr Coffee. Bettr World.' in a yellow (#fcbf27) slab serif at 137 px over dark brown (#2c1c0f); top banner on funding; cookie box over it. Set in Jobclarendon and Roboto.

sites.name: The Quaker School at Horsham
sites.why: First screen is a full-bleed video of two adults helping a child along a balance beam in a classroom, inside a pale blue frame; 'Seen & valued' at 198 px in a Season-family type on cream (#f9f9f0). Menu: Our Approach, Specialist Support, Admissions, Inquire.

sites.name: Primer
sites.why: White (#ffffff) page: a wide cut-out photograph of about 25 children in a line, then a bordered grid with the headline in a serif (Sirca) at 36 px, one sentence and an outlined 'Find a school' button; menu hidden behind a hamburger, black 'Get started' pill top right.

sites.name: Fluently
sites.why: Black (#000000) first screen with a dimmed photograph of a phone on a wooden desk; 64 px white headline 'Speak like you mean it' in DM Sans, one two-line subtitle, App Store and Google Play buttons and a QR code. About 25 words.

sites.name: Krackerz Learning
sites.why: Cream (#f7f6f0) page with a headline in a heavy display face (Highway Motel Sans) at 64 px, a red mascot, one lime 'Join waitlist' button and four tilted photo cards of learners with captions. Colour is red, lime and black.

sites.name: CalArts Graphic Design Yearbook 2026
sites.why: Black (#000000) page, no photograph: 'CALARTS GRAPHIC DESIGN' at 160 px in a heavy condensed sans (Gamay) with a pink brush scribble over it, yellow (#eeff00) year and menu tabs, links to the 2020 to 2025 yearbooks. The work is on sub-pages.

sites.name: 25 Years of University in Zlin
sites.why: Interactive 3D microsite in Czech for the 25th anniversary of Tomas Bata University, with a map of milestones in the city of Zlin; headline 'UTB slaví 25 let' (not seen on a screenshot).

avoid: Stock photos of smiling students at a laptop, and a hero carousel of campus buildings.
A programme list hidden behind a mega-menu or only in a PDF prospectus, so visitors assume the programme does not exist.
Prices, dates and deadlines only after a 'request a brochure' form.
Insider vocabulary (credits, pathways, modules) with no plain explanation for parents and teenagers.
Gimmick copy and slang aimed at young people, instead of clear, age-appropriate content.
Testimonial walls with no names, faces or outcomes, and 'world-class' claims with no figures.
Gamified badges, confetti and mascots on every screen of an adult course platform.
